properties.name: Suscol / Soscol (Mariano G. Vallejo)
properties.summary: About 84,000 acres that General Mariano G. Vallejo bought from Governor Micheltorena in 1843, adjoining his Rancho Petaluma on the west and running east to Rancho Suisun and south to the Carquinez Strait and San Pablo Bay, taking in Mare Island and the sites of the towns Vallejo would sell: Benicia (sold with Larkin and Semple in 1846–47 and named for his wife) and the city of Vallejo, briefly the state capital. The United States rejected the claim: in United States v. Vallejo (1862) the Supreme Court held that the governor had no authority to sell public land, voiding what would have been the largest grant of the north bay.

sources.citation: Diseño: “Map of Suscol” (Bancroft Land Case Maps)
U.S. land-claim case no. 318 (Vallejo, claimant), Northern District of California
Boundary approximate — claim rejected, no U.S. patent

properties.notes: Outline RECONSTRUCTED: its western boundary is drawn along Rancho Petaluma's confirmed eastern edge (the two adjoining Vallejo grants), with the north following the Napa and Suisun grants and the south and east following the Carquinez Strait and San Pablo Bay shoreline, including Mare Island. The rejected claim was never U.S.-surveyed, so this is an approximate reconstruction, not a patent survey.

properties.name: Mare Island / Isla de la Yegua (Victor Castro)
properties.summary: The island of Mare Island (Isla de la Yegua), about 900 acres, granted to Victor Castro — provisionally by the secretary Jimeno in 1840 and in fee by Governor Alvarado in 1841. Castro sold it to John B. Frisbie and B. R. Simmons; the U.S. Navy bought the island in 1853 for its Pacific shipyard. The grant overlapped Vallejo's Suscol claim and its title was likewise contested.
